verdict.rationale: Buzz's architecture is built on open, portable substrates — chat is stored as Nostr events over an open protocol (NIP-29/NIP-42) that any third-party client can read directly, git repos are standard git accessible via git-credential-nostr, and the whole stack is OSS and self-hostable (Helm chart, VPS compose bundle) so a community can 'run your own relay' rather than being locked to Block's hosting. This gives strong architectural openness/portability, but there is no documented explicit bulk 'export my data' command or archive format for a leaving user beyond standing up your own relay/git server. Missing for 10: an explicit data-export CLI/API command, a documented export file format, and independent confirmation that a full self-hosted migration actually preserves history/identity end-to-end.
